title: Zero-inbound network exposure
subtitle: No host in my estate accepts an inbound connection. Everything arrives through authenticated tunnels or a private mesh, and every public surface is fronted by TLS and rate limits.

stats.label: public component in front of a vendor platform: a small edge Worker

lede: Auth and access plane holds my estate to one rule I set early: no service accepts an inbound connection from the internet. Everything public arrives through outbound-only tunnels, one per purpose, separating the main estate, business event intake and the social-platform integrations, so trouble on one surface stays there and I can cut any one surface without touching the others. Where a hosted service needs a public name, NGINX terminates TLS behind the tunnel, and TLS termination, rate limits and security headers sit in that one front layer. Where a vendor platform such as Microsoft Copilot Studio needs a public endpoint, it reaches the tools through an edge Worker.
quote: A service that needs no listener gets none.
evidence: Zero-trust and zero-inbound networking: 0 inbound connections from the internet; everything public arrives through 3 outbound tunnels, one per purpose.
Edge security design: 1 small edge Worker as the only public component in front of a vendor platform, and NGINX with TLS, security headers and per-endpoint rate limits elsewhere.
Mutual TLS for fleet control: LAN GPU workstations bootstrapped by SSH once, then controlled only over mutual TLS with a private certificate authority.
author: Corey James
